subject: High p99 latency + intermittent 500s — production (Poppy Health)

Cc: Poppy Health Engineering <ops@poppyhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High p99 latency + intermittent 500s — production

Hi Naomi / Rishi,

We're seeing a sharp spike in p99 latency over the last ~30 minutes on our production routes (payment-authorization and patient-search). A subset of requests are returning 500s, and the errors seem to correlate with periods of sustained high token generation. Our monitoring shows tail latency jumping from ~180ms to >2.2s and error rate climbing to ~3.5%.

We haven't changed traffic patterns from our side — same RPS — but several of our jobs that hit the same model have higher sequence lengths today. Can your ops/infra team confirm whether anything changed on your side (batching, cache settings, recent rollouts)? This is impacting several patient checkouts; we need guidance and a mitigation plan ASAP.

Attached: a short slice of our request ids and timestamps for traces we captured.

Thanks,
Alyssa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alyssa Reed <alyssa@poppyhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 latency + intermittent 500s — production

Quick update from infra's initial pass. Observations (10:00–10:05 PDT):
- We see repeated KV cache evictions for tenant/poppy (hot keys). Eviction spikes line up with p99 jumps.
- Batch lane formation is stalling: a handful of hot prefixes are occupying hot lanes, causing HOL (head-of-line) blocking for other requests in the same batch lane.
- When eviction churn increases, tails spike and some requests time out and return 500s from the worker when KV lookups fail under backpressure.

What I collected:
- KV cache metrics (attached): per-key hit/miss, eviction-rate, resident-keys.
- Small flame graphs pointing to KV lookup stalls inside the runtime.

Immediate recommendation (safe canary):
1) Apply hot-key isolation (pin the top ~10 hot prefixes for tenant 'poppy' to a separate hot-lane with smaller batch caps).
2) Temporarily reduce max batch window for the affected model to 10ms for Poppy to reduce HOL risk.
3) Increase per-tenant KV cache allocation by ~20% for Poppy's dedicated pool (if they are on Dedicated).

I'll attach the raw CSV with per-key stats. Need Alyssa confirmation to run the canary (we will canary on 5% of traffic first). If Poppy is on shared Hosted, we still can apply lane isolation for that tenant id via routing policy; impact is minimal and reversible.

Attachments: kv_cache-stats-20270418.csv

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 latency + intermittent 500s — production

Thanks Rishi — adding technical context and the operator plan. TL;DR: cache oscillation from a small set of hot prefixes is causing lane starvation and batch stalls. We have two safe, reversible mitigations we can ship in minutes and one medium-term tuning we should schedule.

Operator plan (can be run with your approval):
A) Immediate canary (5% traffic, 15m run):
  - Apply hot-key isolation for top 20 prefixes -> route them to a dedicated hot lane with batch-size cap 4 and max-batch-wait 3ms.
  - Reduce general model max-batch-wait to 10ms for the Poppy tenant routing rule.
  - Monitor p99, error rate, and KV eviction rate. Roll back immediately on adverse changes.

B) Next 24h (if canary looks good):
  - Increase tenant KV reservation by 20%.
  - Deploy a small runtime patch that improves non-blocking KV lookups (low-risk change; patch attached).

Expected impact:
- Short term: p99 should drop towards baseline; some cost increase possible if we reduce batching efficiency for the canary portion.
- Medium term: better tail behavior with minimal throughput loss.

Permission requested: Alyssa — can we run A) now on a 5% canary? We'll provide a dashboard link and a 15-min update.

Attachment: hotkey-isolation.patch.diff

-markus

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 12:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 latency + intermittent 500s — production

Executive summary for leadership: Poppy Health is experiencing a tenant-localized cache oscillation that is producing head-of-line blocking in batch lanes and causing elevated p99s and intermittent 500s. We've proposed a conservative canary (5% traffic, 15m) implementing hot-key isolation + reduced batch-wait for the tenant. Poppy has approved.

Why this matters: if left unchecked the oscillation can cascade into wider lane starvation affecting other tenants on shared pools during high sequence-length workloads. The quick canary is low-risk and reversible. If successful, we will follow up with a 24h KV reservation bump and a runtime patch to make KV lookups non-blocking.

Requested action: please stand by for the 15-minute canary update at ~12:20 PDT. If the canary shows persistent errors or increased cross-tenant impact, we may need to authorize expanded capacity for the affected Dedicated pool.

Naomi
